searchText: Epoch can be recovered from the slot but in general case you may not have access to a chain to recover the checkpoint root from the head root If you don't have the head root then you can't even import the attestation I'd like to join too you don't need to import the attestations to produce attester slashing Oh you mean to slash where you don't know one of the branches? yes, produce slashing and then process it I believe we can remove `epoch` from target checkpoint, this is because we can assume that slots per epoch will never change in the existing protocol. Or if they change `epoch` can be easily recoverable anyway Do you need the checkpoint for slashings? Both double votes and surroundings can be checked with the slot and blockroot you're right, blockroot can replace checkpoint root an important property is that checkpoint root implies a certain blockroot now i am thinking about the case when attestation is included into a competing fork which doesn't know about a blockroot while the checkpoint is known it isn't possible to process an attestation in this case unless a checkpoint root is explicitly included yes, processing of attestations would have to be different, but it's not clear to me that we care about this on-chain component, as long as the off-chain component in forkchoice is fine it's not clear to me the impact of the on-chain part
